meta.methodology: Read framework.md, all reference===125 edges from torahData.js (none found), and the full source text torah_125.txt. Scanned all 6 lines of source text for bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, לְשׁוֹן) per framework guidelines. Checked every instance of 'הַיְנוּ' and 'לְרַמֵּז' for whether they function as bechina declarations of shared essential nature between two distinct concepts.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The word 'הַיּוֹם' is the anchoring scriptural word from which the entire teaching is derived (Exodus 16:25, with three occurrences). However, the Torah does not establish 'today' as a bechina of any other concept — it is the halakhic peg for the ruling about three Shabbat meals and the motivation for eating only for the present. No bechina relationship is stated.

The teaching is about the obligation to eat three Shabbat meals, derived from the threefold repetition of 'today'. The Rebbe does not equate three meals with any other domain via bechina language. This is a halakhic derivation (midrash), not a bechina equivalence.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: הַיְנוּ סְעֻדָּה זוֹ לֹא בִּשְׁבִיל קֹדֶם וְלֹא בִּשְׁבִיל אַחַר-כָּךְ (this meal not for before or after)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 3 uses 'הַיְנוּ' to gloss the meaning of 'for today' — 'meaning: this meal is not for before or after'. This is explanatory apposition (definition), not a bechina statement. The framework requires 'X הוא בחינת Y' — X is an aspect of Y sharing the same essential nature. Here the Rebbe is saying what 'for today' means in behavioral terms, not equating two distinct conceptual domains. No bechina relationship is stated.

Line 3 says the threefold 'today' comes 'to hint' (לְרַמֵּז) that one should eat only for the present. 'לְרַמֵּז' introduces a homiletical reading of the scriptural repetition, not a bechina (shared-essence) equation between concepts. Excluded per framework strictness rule.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: אֲכִילַת שַׁבָּת הִיא כֻּלָּהּ אֱלֹקוּת כֻּלָּהּ קֹדֶשׁ (Shabbat eating is entirely divine, entirely holy)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: This statement in line 5 (editor's note) is the Rebbe's own later clarification that Shabbat eating is holy. It uses 'הִיא' (is) but in a declarative-qualitative sense ('it is entirely holiness'), not the technical bechina formula 'X הוא בחינת Y' equating two distinct conceptual domains. Furthermore, it appears in the editor's bracketed note, not in the Rebbe's actual Torah. Excluded.
